extracted.intended_audience: television writers, producers, casting directors, talent agents, and industry observers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and observations about TV pilot development, casting, and production strategies in a changing industry landscape (year‑round development, streaming/digital players, limited series). Useful for producers, writers, and casting professionals planning projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year‑round development cycle / cable model
rubrics_metrics.description: "Broadcast executives for years have been preaching about switching to a year‑round development cycle or adopting the cable model of producing fewer pilots with higher pilot‑to‑series ratio."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a year‑round development approach or focus on fewer, higher‑quality pilots to increase pilot‑to‑series conversion. The piece notes that despite calls to change, the traditional pilot season paradigm has not yet been fully broken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of off‑cycle pilots and opportunistic late‑season orders
rubrics_metrics.description: "They have been ordering occasional off‑cycle pilots and have jumped on scripts with pilot orders in November and December but are yet to break the traditional pilot season paradigm."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordering off‑cycle pilots or taking late opportunities can supplement development, but these tactics alone have not replaced the established pilot season; expect hybrid behavior from networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for a continuous pilot season
rubrics_metrics.description: "In 2013, we had what was probably the first true continuous pilot season, with existing and new cable and digital players constantly handing out pilot and straight‑to‑series orders."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production, casting, and agent workflows should be prepared for year‑round activity: ongoing casting, auditions, and development rather than concentrated seasonal bursts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue limited/event series opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: "Add to that the new push into limited/event series arena..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developing limited or event series is a growing strategy for networks and streamers; these formats can fit new platform strategies and may require different casting, scheduling, and writing approaches than traditional multi‑season shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize casting availability as a limiting factor
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every year, there are a handful of pilots that are left unproduced because of difficulty casting. There is quiet panic in the air these days that this coming pilot season we will see a lot more of that."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Casting shortages can sink pilots; producers should anticipate competition for actors, lock talent earlier when possible, and design projects with realistic casting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for writer shortage, especially in drama
rubrics_metrics.description: "The proliferation of scripted programming across different platforms caused a shortage of writers, especially on the drama side, pushing the number of drama buys this development season way down."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect fewer drama buys and increased competition for experienced writers; consider alternative staffing models, development timelines, or genre shifts to adapt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on cancelled series to free up talent
rubrics_metrics.description: "A cancelled series used to mean a cast available for the following broadcast pilot season... Now actors from cancelled shows are snatched long before the following broadcast pilot season rolls along."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers should not assume cast availability after cancellations; secure talent earlier and be aware that emerging players may recruit actors immediately after cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target and engage emerging scripted outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: "Other new outlets greenlighting scripted pilots and series now are Netflix, Bravo, E!, DirecTV, We TV, xBox and Hulu. We also saw a rapid rise in ambitious, multi‑series/movie‑to‑series packages... Amazon alone ordered and cast some 13 comedy and drama pilots this past year."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand pitching and development efforts beyond traditional broadcast/cable to include streaming and digital platforms; these players are significant buyers of pilots and straight‑to‑series orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for large franchise/multi‑series packages
rubrics_metrics.description: "rapid rise in ambitious, multi‑series/movie‑to‑series packages, like Marvel’s 60‑episode, four‑series and mini‑series... All those projects will be looking for casts."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large franchise deals create substantial casting and production opportunities but also increase competition and long‑term commitment expectations; tailor submissions and talent searches to fit these large‑scale formats.
